ai.title: Fix CLI paste handling and readline buffer
ai.summary: CLI paste handling and readline buffer fixed. Logic prevents double-space-to-newline conversion during active paste sessions. Internal readline buffer clearing syntax adjusted. Scope limited to npm-app/src/cli.ts.

eli5.text: When you paste text into the command-line tool, double spaces used to turn into unwanted line breaks. Now the tool waits until the paste finishes before converting double spaces to new lines, so your pasted content stays intact. This only affects people typing commands into the terminal interface.

ai.title: calculate-mrr script now counts pastdue subscriptions
ai.summary: calculate-mrr.ts adds a second pagination loop for Stripe subscriptions with status 'past_due', accumulating totalPastDueMRR and totalPastDueInvoices separately from active subscriptions. Previously the script only queried active subscriptions, undercounting MRR when payments failed but the subscription remained in a past_due state. Scope limited to scripts/calculate-mrr.ts; calculate-average-spend.ts received formatting cleanup and a ts-pattern import but no behavioral change. Past due base prices are matched via item.price.recurring?.usage_type === 'licensed', identical to the active subscription logic.

eli5.text: Your company's monthly revenue report now includes money from subscribers whose payments failed but whose subscriptions are still active. If a subscriber's card was declined or their payment bounced, they previously didn't count toward the monthly revenue total even though they still had access to your service; now those 'past due' subscriptions are added to the report separately. You would notice this by seeing a new line in the revenue summary labeled for past due subscriptions, showing both the count of those subscriptions and the revenue they represent.

ai.title: system-prompt: codesearch for refs, .md planning files
ai.summary: backend/src/system-prompt.ts swaps grep for code_search when locating references to modified exported tokens. Adds directive for agent to create structured .md files during planning or design discussions. Internal prompt logic change. No user-facing surface or version impact.

eli5.text: The internal assistant now finds references to renamed or changed code using the project's built-in code search tool instead of a simple text scan, so it catches more of the spots that need updating. When the assistant starts helping you plan a feature or work through a design, it will save that planning discussion into a structured markdown (.md) file with clear sections, instead of leaving the plan only in the conversation.

ai.title: runTerminalCommand reset shell instead of throw
ai.summary: runTerminalCommand in npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts calls resetShell() when commandIsRunning is true, replacing the throw new Error('Command is already running'). Prevents errors on concurrent commands. Scope limited to terminal utility.

eli5.text: When you try to run a new terminal command while another command is still running, instead of throwing an error and crashing, the system now just resets the terminal and runs the new command. This affects anyone using the command-line tool in the application - they won't see error messages when they accidentally trigger two commands at once. You would notice that commands now succeed instead of failing with 'command already running' errors. This change is live today in the application.

ai.title: Fix hydration error on referrals page
ai.summary: Refactored JSX structure in `web/src/app/referrals/page.tsx` to resolve hydration mismatch. Removed redundant `CardContent` wrapper and nested `div` elements within the referral link section. Simplified `CardDescription` layout by stripping unnecessary flex container.

eli5.text: You may have noticed the referrals page (the page showing your invite links and earned credits) occasionally showed a blank area or misaligned content when it first loaded. That happened because the page built its layout slightly differently on the first load versus when it updated, which is called a hydration error. The page's layout pieces were simplified: a stray wrapper that held the 'Share this link' input box and its copy button was dropped, and the text explaining the referral bonus and your referred-friend count lost an unnecessary extra container. If you open the referrals page again now, the invite link and the explanation about both you and your friend earning credits will render consistently from the start instead of flickering or appearing empty during load.

ai.title: Ignore .codebuff hidden folder in .gitignore
ai.summary: Added `.codebuff*` to `.gitignore` to exclude hidden `.codebuff` folders from version control. This prevents local agent state files from being accidentally committed. Affects repository configuration only.

eli5.text: Your project's hidden assistant folder, which keeps track of the assistant's local working state, will no longer be accidentally saved and shared back into the project's shared file list. This only touches the project's settings file that decides what gets stored. No features for you will change.

ai.title: Rename npm package codebuff to codecane and bump version to 1.0.152
ai.summary: The `npm-app` package name changes from `codebuff` to `codecane`, updating the `bin` entry accordingly. Version bumps from 1.0.149 to 1.0.152. This rename affects the CLI binary command name and package identity.

eli5.text: Your AI coding assistant now answers to a new name: instead of typing 'codebuff' to talk to it from the command line, you'll type 'codecane'. The software also got a small update (1.0.152), which includes a handful of fixes like better handling when you paste text into the terminal and a corrected bug affecting one of the app's pages. If you use the assistant through the terminal or command prompts, you'll need to use the new name going forward.

ai.title: Revert version bump to 1.0.149 in npm-app
ai.summary: Reverts version bump in npm-app/package.json from 1.0.152 to 1.0.149. Also reverts package name from codecane to codebuff. Scope limited to npm-app/package.json.

eli5.text: The team rolled back a recent update to the AI assistant's name and version number. This change affects internal tools and has no impact on the daily experience of current users.
